_: Name, description and badge live in src/resources/connectors.json so the console and the browser process cannot disagree about them.

shape.note: Superhuman Mail publishes NO REST API. The only programmatic surface is an MCP server, so this is the one connector in the catalogue Flux does not call over HTTP itself - it attaches the server to the agent and the agent calls tools. That is why its transport is `mcp` rather than `api`, and why the operations below have tool names instead of methods and paths.
shape.not_to_be_confused_with: Superhuman Docs, which is the rebranded Coda and has a full REST API at coda.io/apis/v1. Different product, different connector - see data/connectors/coda.json. Superhuman also ships Go (AI agents) and Grammarly under the same brand.

auth.mechanism: Browser sign-in. The Superhuman Mail Chrome extension performs the authentication; no key, token or client secret is issued to the caller, and Flux stores no credential for this connector.
notes: Nothing to paste and nothing to put in the OS keychain - the whole reason this connector's setup flow differs from every other one.

Adding a second mailbox is done by asking the agent, which calls add_account and returns a one-time sign-in link. That link is a live credential in URL form: it must never be forwarded to anyone, and a link arriving from someone else must never be opened. Superhuman says so twice on their own page and the console should repeat it at the point the link is produced.
An account being added must already be on the user's own seat. Linking someone else's address fails.

requirements: A Superhuman Mail account with Ask AI enabled.
The Superhuman Mail Chrome extension installed - it is what authenticates the session.
A Business plan or higher. The MCP server is not available on Starter, so a Starter user cannot connect this at all and the console should say that rather than failing at sign-in.
On Enterprise or otherwise managed accounts an admin may have to enable MCP access first, arranged through the customer's CSM. Not every managed account requires it.

api.note: Deliberately null. There is no HTTP base URL to record - see `shape`.

query_email_and_calendar.label: Search email and calendar
query_email_and_calendar.notes: Semantic search in natural language across mail and calendar. The right first call for an open-ended question.

list_threads.label: List threads
list_threads.notes: Structured filters - From, To, Subject, Labels, Split, date. Prefer this over the semantic search when the filter is known, since it is deterministic.

get_thread.label: Get a thread
get_thread.notes: Full thread including messages, drafts and comments.

list_splits.label: List splits
list_splits.notes: Split Inboxes, e.g. Important and Other.

get_availability.label: Get availability
get_availability.notes: Free time across a set of participants.

get_read_statuses.label: Get read statuses
get_read_statuses.notes: Who opened a sent email, when, and on what device. It is the user's own read-tracking data, but it is data about other people - worth surfacing in a summary only when the task actually asked for it.

list_accounts.label: List accounts
list_accounts.notes: Which mailboxes are linked and which is default. Worth calling first on any multi-account request: tools act on the default account unless told otherwise, so a search that looks empty is often a search of the wrong inbox.

create_or_update_draft.label: Create or update a draft
create_or_update_draft.notes: Writes in the user's voice using their Personalization settings. Drafts created here appear in Superhuman Mail; drafts made in Gmail or Outlook do not, and vice versa.

create_or_update_event.label: Create or update an event
create_or_update_event.notes: Scoped as `send`, not `draft`, on purpose: creating or moving a meeting mails invitations to the other attendees. It is outbound whatever it is called.

send_draft.label: Send a draft
send_draft.notes: Sends immediately with no built-in delay. Superhuman's own guidance is to require confirmation on every call, and Flux must do that rather than relying on the client's tool-approval settings. Supports Smart Send (deliver when the recipient is most likely to open it), Scheduled Send, and Undo Send.

undo_send.label: Undo send
undo_send.notes: Cancels a send inside the undo window. Recorded as a write rather than readonly because it changes state, but it only ever retracts - it is the safe half of send_draft and should stay available wherever send_draft is.

never_expose: trash_thread and update_thread - update_thread looks like harmless labelling but its documented actions include moving a thread to Trash, so the two carry the same risk.
discard_draft - deletes a draft the user may have written by hand.
unsubscribe - it also offers Trash and Block, and unsubscribing from a list on someone's behalf is a decision, not a chore.
update_personalization - rewrites the writing style and stored facts that every future draft is generated from. An agent editing its own prompt is not something to do silently.
add_account and remove_account - account linking is a credential operation and belongs in the console's own setup flow, in front of the user, not in a tool call the agent can reach mid-task.
set_default_account - silently changes which mailbox every later call acts on.
gotchas: Every tool acts on the default account unless the account is named. A cross-account question needs to say so explicitly, or it quietly answers from one inbox.
Superhuman's own advice is to name the MCP tool in the prompt for reliable results, which suggests the tool descriptions alone do not always route correctly.
Attachments can be read but the documentation gives no way to attach one when sending.

also_ships.skills: Superhuman publishes a skills library at github.com/superhuman/mcp-mail/tree/main/skills - Morning Briefing, End of Day Wrap-Up, Batch Draft Writer, Deal Tracker, Meeting Scheduler. These overlap directly with several entries in data/skills, and are worth reading before writing a Superhuman skill of our own rather than after.

notes: The tool list, the plan and extension prerequisites, the send-confirmation advice and the sign-in-link warning are taken verbatim from Superhuman's own help centre article.
The write_scope on each tool is Flux's own judgement, not Superhuman's - they publish no such classification. create_or_update_event is deliberately rated `send`.

The client-by-client connection steps in that article render as empty numbered lists in the text form supplied, so the actual MCP server URL and the per-client command lines are NOT recorded here. They are needed before the console can wire this up - see the note in connectors.json.
